latestRelease.title: v1.40.1
latestRelease.notes:
## This is a patch release.

### What's Changed

- Fixed connection-state handling in squashed pipelines. Commands following `AUTH`, `SELECT`, `HELLO`, `CLIENT`, or `RESET` now observe the updated connection state instead of stale authentication, database, or RESP protocol state ([#8016](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/pull/8016)).
- Fixed compressed QList node memory accounting and defragmentation ([#8011](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/pull/8011), [#8014](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/pull/8014)).

Full Changelog: [v1.40.0...v1.40.1](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/compare/v1.40.0...v1.40.1)
highlights: Fixed connection-state handling in squashed pipelines. Commands following AUTH, SELECT, HELLO, CLIENT, or RESET now observe the updated connection state instead of stale authentication, database, or RESP protocol state (#8016).
Fixed compressed QList node memory accounting and defragmentation (#8011, #8014).

signals.title: ZMPOP RESP2 reply is incompatibile with Redis
signals.text:
# `ZMPOP` returns the wrong RESP2 null type when no member can be popped **NOTE**: I found this issue when adding `dragonfly` to PhpRedis' CI (https://github.com/phpredis/phpredis/pull/2907). This surfaced about half a dozen reply shape incompatibilities with Redis. If perfect compatibility isn't a goal of dragonfly just let me know and I can instead update our tests **Describe the bug** When no member can be popped, Dragonfly returns a RESP2 null bulk string (`$-1
`) instead of the null array (`*-1
`) returned by Redis. RESP2 null bulk strings and null arrays are distinct wire types even though some clients map both to the same language-level value. PhpRedis parses `ZMPOP` with its multi-bulk response parser. Dragonfly's null bulk string does not match the expected aggregate response type, so PhpRedis rejects the response and returns `false` instead of the expected empty result or `null`. **To Reproduce** 1. Connect using RESP2 to databases where `zs` does not exist or is empty. 2. Run `ZMPOP 1 zs MIN` against Redis and Dragonfly. 3. Compare the wire responses. In the example below, port 6379 is Redis and port 9999 is Dragonfly. ```console $ printf 'ZMPOP 1 zs MIN
' | nc -N localhost 6379 *-1 $ printf 'ZMPOP 1 zs MIN
' | nc -N localhost 9999 $-1 ``` **Expected behavior** Like Redis, Dragonfly should return a RESP2 null array: ```text *-1
 ``` `ZMPOP` otherwise returns an aggregate containing the selected key and popped members, so its nil result should retain the aggregate response type. **Screenshots** Not applicable; the raw protocol responses are included above. **Environment (please complete the following information):** - OS: Not recorded - Kernel: Not recorded - Containerized?: Not recorded - Dragonfly Version: `df-v1.39.0` Redis control version: `8.9.241` Protocol: RESP2 **Reproducible Code Snippet** ```sh printf 'ZMPOP 1 zs MIN
' | nc -N localhost 9999 ``` **Additional context** With `Redis::OPT_NULL_MULTIBULK_AS_NULL` enabled, PhpRedis recognizes a null array as an empty `ZMPOP` result and returns it to PHP as `null`. This mismatch causes `Redis_Test::testZmpop` to fail: ```text Assertion failed: testZmpop - (false) !== (null) ``` Dragonfly's `ZMPopGeneric` empty-result path calls `SendNull()`: - [ZMPOP implementation](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/src/server/zset_family.cc) - [RESP reply builder](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/src/facade/reply_builder.cc) For RESP2, `SendNull()` emits `$-1
`. The reply builder has a distinct `SendNullArray()` method which emits `*-1
`. Dragonfly also returns `$-1
` for an empty or timed-out `BZMPOP`. The current PhpRedis `testBZmpop` only asserts the default `false` result, so it does not expose the type mismatch through `OPT_NULL_MULTIBULK_AS_NULL`.

signals.title: ZADD GT/LT are silently ignored once a sorted set leaves listpack encoding
signals.text:
## Summary `ZADD ... GT` and `ZADD ... LT` are silently ignored for sorted sets that are not listpack-encoded. The flag is dropped with no error and the command behaves like a plain `ZADD`, so the score is overwritten unconditionally. Two independent conditions push a zset out of listpack encoding, and either one is enough to trigger this: - any member longer than **32 bytes** - more than **128 members** `NX` continues to behave correctly on the same keys, so this looks specific to GT/LT handling rather than to option parsing in general. Reproduced on **v1.39.0** and **v1.40.1** (latest at time of writing). Redis 7.4.10 is correct in every case, including at `skiplist` encoding. ## Reproduction ``` $ redis-cli DEL k $ redis-cli ZADD k GT 10 aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa # 33-byte member, inserts $ redis-cli ZADD k GT 3 aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa # must be a no-op: 3 < 10 $ redis-cli ZSCORE k aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa "3" # expected "10" ``` The same member at 32 bytes returns `"10"` as expected. A self-contained script covering both boundaries and the `NX` contrast case: ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash set -u IMAGE="${1:-docker.dragonflydb.io/dragonflydb/dragonfly:v1.40.1}" NAME="zadd_gtlt_repro_$$" docker rm -f "$NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 if [[ "$IMAGE" == *dragonfly* ]]; then docker run -d --name "$NAME" "$IMAGE" --logtostderr >/dev/null else docker run -d --name "$NAME" "$IMAGE" >/dev/null fi sleep 4 C() { docker exec "$NAME" redis-cli "$@"; } echo "server: $(C INFO server | grep -E 'dragonfly_version|redis_version' | tr -d '')" fail=0 check() { local label="$1" flag="$2" first="$3" second="$4" expect="$5" member="$6" local key="k$RANDOM$RANDOM" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null C ZADD "$key" "$flag" "$first" "$member" >/dev/null # insert C ZADD "$key" "$flag" "$second" "$member" >/dev/null # must NOT apply local got; got=$(C ZSCORE "$key" "$member" | tr -d '') local status=OK if [[ "$got" != "$expect" ]]; then status=BROKEN; fail=1; fi printf ' %-34s ZADD %s %-5s -> %-5s (want %-5s) %s
' \ "$label" "$flag" "$second" "$got" "$expect" "$status" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null } echo "--- member length ---" check "1-byte member" GT 10 3 10 "x" check "32-byte member" GT 10 3 10 "$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..32})" check "33-byte member" GT 10 3 10 "$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..33})" check "33-byte member" LT 3 10 3 "$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..33})" echo "--- member count (all members 2 bytes) ---" for count in 128 129; do key="c$count" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null { for i in $(seq 1 "$count"); do echo "ZADD $key GT 10 m$i"; done; } \ | docker exec -i "$NAME" redis-cli >/dev/null C ZADD "$key" GT 3 m1 >/dev/null got=$(C ZSCORE "$key" m1 | tr -d '') status=OK if [[ "$got" != "10" ]]; then status=BROKEN; fail=1; fi printf ' %-34s ZADD GT 3 -> %-5s (want 10 ) %s
' "$count members" "$got" "$status" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null done echo "--- NX on a 33-byte member, for contrast ---" key="nx$RANDOM"; M="$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..33})" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null C ZADD "$key" 10 "$M" >/dev/null C ZADD "$key" NX 3 "$M" >/dev/null got=$(C ZSCORE "$key" "$M" | tr -d '') printf ' %-34s ZADD NX 3 -> %-5s (want 10 ) %s
' "33-byte member" "$got" \ "$([[ "$got" == 10 ]] && echo OK || echo BROKEN)" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null docker rm -f "$NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 echo [[ $fail -eq 0 ]] && echo "RESULT: all GT/LT clamps held" || echo "RESULT: GT/LT ignored in some encodings" exit $fail ``` ## Observed output Dragonfly v1.40.1 (identical on v1.39.0): ``` server: redis_version:7.4.0 dragonfly_version:df-v1.40.1 --- member length --- 1-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 32-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 33-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 3 (want 10 ) BROKEN 33-byte member ZADD LT 10 -> 10 (want 3 ) BROKEN --- member count (all members 2 bytes) --- 128 members ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 129 members ZADD GT 3 -> 3 (want 10 ) BROKEN --- NX on a 33-byte member, for contrast --- 33-byte member ZADD NX 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK RESULT: GT/LT ignored in some encodings ``` Redis 7.4.10, same script: ``` server: redis_version:7.4.10 --- member length --- 1-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 32-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 33-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 33-byte member ZADD LT 10 -> 3 (want 3 ) OK --- member count (all members 2 bytes) --- 128 members ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 129 members ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK --- NX on a 33-byte member, for contrast --- 33-byte member ZADD NX 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK RESULT: all GT/LT clamps held ``` ## Expected behaviour Per the `ZADD` contract, `GT` updates an existing member only if the new score is greater than the current one, and `LT` only if it is less. Neither prevents inserting an absent member. This should hold regardless of the internal encoding. ## Environment - Dragonfly `v1.39.0` and `v1.40.1`, official images, default flags plus `--logtostderr` - Docker on macOS (arm64) - Reference: `redis:7.4-alpine` (7.4.10), default config ## Why this matters `ZADD GT`/`LT` is the only native atomic max/min in the Redis API, so it is the natural primitive for tracking running extrema without a read-modify-write or a Lua script. Because the flag is dropped silently rather than rejected, the failure surfaces as plausible-looking but wrong data — a stored extremum becomes "the most recently written value" — and only for keys that happen to have grown past a threshold. There is no error and no metric to alert on. Small smoke tests will pass, which makes this easy to adopt and hard to detect: we validated the primitive with short members on an empty key, built on it, and only caught the problem when a concurrency test on realistic key shapes reported a minimum of 919.5 where the true minimum was 81. Rejecting GT/LT with an error on unsupported encodings would at least be safe, but matching Redis semantics is obviously preferable.

signals.title: feat(geo): add GEOSEARCHSTORE command
signals.text: <!-- **Commits Must Be Signed and Your PR title must conform to the conventional commit spec** * See: https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md * Please follow the section on `pre-commit hooks`, a linter will validate before you push Example PR Title: <type>(<scope>)!: <description> * `type` = bug, chore, feat, fix, docs, build, style, refactor, perf, test * `!` = OPTIONAL: signals a breaking change * `scope` = Optional when `type` is "chore" or "docs" * `description` = short description of the change Examples: * chore(examples): Clarify `docker` usage #120 * docs(readme): Fix Example Links #121 * feat(ingest)!: Add new ingest #122 * fix(ingest): Refactor for loop to list comprehension #123 --> Adds GEOSEARCHSTORE (dest + src keys, same search options as GEOSEARCH, optional STOREDIST). Most of the work was already in GeoSearchStoreGeneric() via GEORADIUS ... STORE — this wires up the dedicated command and parser. Closes #3883. Also fixed a couple of Redis mismatches in the shared store/search path: - STORE when the source key is missing now returns 0 and clears the dest key (was an empty array) - COUNT without ASC/DESC now defaults to ASC, same as Redis Tests in geo_family_test.cc. Ran geo_family_test locally + manual redis-cli checks.

signals.title: fix(server): lower table growth margin default
signals.text: ## Summary - Lower the default `table_growth_margin` from `0.4` to `0.15`. - Reduce the conservative free-capacity estimate before allowing table growth. ## Test plan - `git diff --check` passed. - `ninja -C build-dbg dragonfly` reached and compiled `src/server/db_slice.cc`; the full build was blocked by the host filesystem running out of space.
signals.author: romange

signals.title: fix(server): probe heterogeneous blocking waiters instead of aborting…
signals.text: ## Summary `BlockingController` keeps one FIFO queue per `(db, key)` shared by *all* blocking commands watching that key. `NotifyWatchQueue()` only checked the front waiter: when its checker returned `kKeyNotFound` (e.g. `BLPOP`/`BZPOP*`/`BLMPOP` on a missing key), the scan aborted entirely and the one-shot wake event was cleared, so any *later* waiter in the same queue, from a different command family, was never checked at all. Concretely: a client blocked on `XREADGROUP` queued behind an earlier `BLPOP` waiter on the same key would never receive its `NOGROUP` error when the key was deleted. It stayed blocked indefinitely, only released later by an unrelated mutation of the key. ## Fix `NotifyWatchQueue` no longer aborts the whole scan on `kKeyNotFound`. It now tracks the checker (command family) that reported the key missing, and only fast-skips *later* waiters sharing that exact checker, this preserves the O (1)-per-item short-circuit from #7225 for the common homogeneous case (many `BLPOP` waiters on one absent key). Waiters from a different command family (e.g. `XREADGROUP` sharing a queue with `BLPOP`) are still probed individually, so they get the correct, immediate result instead of being hidden behind an unrelated waiter's outcome. ## Test plan - [x] New regression test `BlockingControllerTest.NotifyWatchQueueHeterogeneousCheckers`- two waiters with different checker types on one key's queue; the first reports `kKeyNotFound`, and the test asserts the second is still probed. - [x] Existing `BlockingControllerTest.NotifyWatchQueueFastPathOnAbsentKey` (the #7225 perf regression test) still passes unmodified, same-checker-type fast path is preserved. - [x] `blocking_controller_test`, `stream_family_test`, `list_family_test`, `zset_family_test` all passes. - [x] `pre-commit` (clang-format et al.) clean. Fixes #8067
signals.author: Shikha-code36

signals.title: fix(zset): honor GT/LT flags for skiplist-encoded sorted sets
signals.text: ## Summary `ZADD ... GT` and `ZADD ... LT` were silently ignored once a sorted set left listpack encoding (i.e. once it had a member longer than 32 bytes, or more than 128 members). The score was overwritten unconditionally, as if the command were a plain `ZADD`, with no error. Root cause: the GT/LT clamp check exists in the listpack path (`ZsetAdd` in `zset_family.cc`) but was missing entirely from the skiplist path (`SortedMap::AddElem` in `sorted_map.cc`), which just updated the score whenever the element already existed. ## Fix Add the same GT/LT clamp to `SortedMap::AddElem`: if `LT` and the new score isn't lower, or `GT` and the new score isn't higher, treat the update as a no-op (matching the listpack path and Redis semantics). ## Test plan - Added `ZSetFamilyTest.AddGtLtSkiplist`, using a 33-byte member to force skiplist encoding immediately, covering both GT and LT in both the no-op and update directions. - `ninja zset_family_test && ./zset_family_test --gtest_filter='*GtLt*:*Add*'` — all 5 tests pass. - `pre-commit` clang-format check passes on both changed files. Fixes #8089
signals.author: Shikha-code36

signals.title: fix: reply with a null array for empty ZMPOP/BZMPOP/LMPOP/BLMPOP
signals.text: When no element can be popped, ZMPOP/BZMPOP/LMPOP/BLMPOP replied with a RESP2 null bulk string (`$-1\r\n`) instead of the null array (`*-1\r\n`) expected for aggregate-reply commands, so strict clients (e.g. PhpRedis) rejected the reply. Changes: - `RedisReplyBuilderBase::SendNullArray()` is now protocol-aware: `*-1` under RESP2, `_` under RESP3 (previously it always emitted `*-1`, a legacy RESP2 encoding). - The empty/timeout reply paths of ZMPOP/BZMPOP (`zset_family.cc`) and LMPOP/BLMPOP (`list_family.cc`) use `SendNullArray()`. - BLMPOP now maps non-OK statuses the same way BLPOP does; a `WRONGTYPE` error is no longer swallowed into a null reply. - `InterpreterReplier::SendNullArray()` converts a null-array reply to Lua `false` (previously it produced an empty table and called `PostItem()` twice, which hit a DCHECK in debug builds when reached, e.g. via `EVAL` calling `XINFO STREAM` on an empty stream). - Tests: existing empty/timeout assertions now expect the null array; added a BLMPOP wrong-type test, a RESP3 `SendNullArray` byte test, a Lua conversion test, and a raw-socket pytest asserting the exact wire bytes under RESP2 and RESP3. Intentional side effect: Blocking-timeout and no-data replies of BLPOP/BRPOP, BZPOPMIN/BZPOPMAX, XREAD/XREADGROUP, and XINFO STREAM's empty `first-entry`/`last-entry` now emit the protocol-correct `_` instead of the legacy `*-1` under RESP3. RESP2 bytes for those commands are unchanged. Fixes #8087
signals.author: vyavdoshenko

Reproduced on **v1.39.0** and **v1.40.1** (latest at time of writing). Redis 7.4.10 is correct in every case, including at `skiplist` encoding. ## Reproduction ``` $ redis-cli DEL k $ redis-cli ZADD k GT 10 aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa # 33-byte member, inserts $ redis-cli ZADD k GT 3 aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa # must be a no-op: 3 < 10 $ redis-cli ZSCORE k aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa "3" # expected "10" ``` The same member at 32 bytes returns `"10"` as expected. A self-contained script covering both boundaries and the `NX` contrast case: ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash set -u IMAGE="${1:-docker.dragonflydb.io/dragonflydb/dragonfly:v1.40.1}" NAME="zadd_gtlt_repro_$$" docker rm -f "$NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 if [[ "$IMAGE" == *dragonfly* ]]; then docker run -d --name "$NAME" "$IMAGE" --logtostderr >/dev/null else docker run -d --name "$NAME" "$IMAGE" >/dev/null fi sleep 4 C() { docker exec "$NAME" redis-cli "$@"; } echo "server: $(C INFO server | grep -E 'dragonfly_version|redis_version' | tr -d '')" fail=0 check() { local label="$1" flag="$2" first="$3" second="$4" expect="$5" member="$6" local key="k$RANDOM$RANDOM" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null C ZADD "$key" "$flag" "$first" "$member" >/dev/null # insert C ZADD "$key" "$flag" "$second" "$member" >/dev/null # must NOT apply local got; got=$(C ZSCORE "$key" "$member" | tr -d '') local status=OK if [[ "$got" != "$expect" ]]; then status=BROKEN; fail=1; fi printf ' %-34s ZADD %s %-5s -> %-5s (want %-5s) %s
' \ "$label" "$flag" "$second" "$got" "$expect" "$status" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null } echo "--- member length ---" check "1-byte member" GT 10 3 10 "x" check "32-byte member" GT 10 3 10 "$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..32})" check "33-byte member" GT 10 3 10 "$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..33})" check "33-byte member" LT 3 10 3 "$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..33})" echo "--- member count (all members 2 bytes) ---" for count in 128 129; do key="c$count" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null { for i in $(seq 1 "$count"); do echo "ZADD $key GT 10 m$i"; done; } \ | docker exec -i "$NAME" redis-cli >/dev/null C ZADD "$key" GT 3 m1 >/dev/null got=$(C ZSCORE "$key" m1 | tr -d '') status=OK if [[ "$got" != "10" ]]; then status=BROKEN; fail=1; fi printf ' %-34s ZADD GT 3 -> %-5s (want 10 ) %s
' "$count members" "$got" "$status" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null done echo "--- NX on a 33-byte member, for contrast ---" key="nx$RANDOM"; M="$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..33})" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null C ZADD "$key" 10 "$M" >/dev/null C ZADD "$key" NX 3 "$M" >/dev/null got=$(C ZSCORE "$key" "$M" | tr -d '') printf ' %-34s ZADD NX 3 -> %-5s (want 10 ) %s
' "33-byte member" "$got" \ "$([[ "$got" == 10 ]] && echo OK || echo BROKEN)" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null docker rm -f "$NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 echo [[ $fail -eq 0 ]] && echo "RESULT: all GT/LT clamps held" || echo "RESULT: GT/LT ignored in some encodings" exit $fail ``` ## Observed output Dragonfly v1.40.1 (identical on v1.39.0): ``` server: redis_version:7.4.0 dragonfly_version:df-v1.40.1 --- member length --- 1-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 32-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 33-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 3 (want 10 ) BROKEN 33-byte member ZADD LT 10 -> 10 (want 3 ) BROKEN --- member count (all members 2 bytes) --- 128 members ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 129 members ZADD GT 3 -> 3 (want 10 ) BROKEN --- NX on a 33-byte member, for contrast --- 33-byte member ZADD NX 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK RESULT: GT/LT ignored in some encodings ``` Redis 7.4.10, same script: ``` server: redis_version:7.4.10 --- member length --- 1-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 32-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 33-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 33-byte member ZADD LT 10 -> 3 (want 3 ) OK --- member count (all members 2 bytes) --- 128 members ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 129 members ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK --- NX on a 33-byte member, for contrast --- 33-byte member ZADD NX 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK RESULT: all GT/LT clamps held ``` ## Expected behaviour Per the `ZADD` contract, `GT` updates an existing member only if the new score is greater than the current one, and `LT` only if it is less. Neither prevents inserting an absent member. This should hold regardless of the internal encoding. ## Environment - Dragonfly `v1.39.0` and `v1.40.1`, official images, default flags plus `--logtostderr` - Docker on macOS (arm64) - Reference: `redis:7.4-alpine` (7.4.10), default config ## Why this matters `ZADD GT`/`LT` is the only native atomic max/min in the Redis API, so it is the natural primitive for tracking running extrema without a read-modify-write or a Lua script. Because the flag is dropped silently rather than rejected, the failure surfaces as plausible-looking but wrong data — a stored extremum becomes "the most recently written value" — and only for keys that happen to have grown past a threshold. There is no error and no metric to alert on. Small smoke tests will pass, which makes this easy to adopt and hard to detect: we validated the primitive with short members on an empty key, built on it, and only caught the problem when a concurrency test on realistic key shapes reported a minimum of 919.5 where the true minimum was 81. Rejecting GT/LT with an error on unsupported encodings would at least be safe, but matching Redis semantics is obviously preferable.

signal.title: fix(server): probe heterogeneous blocking waiters instead of aborting…
signal.text: ## Summary `BlockingController` keeps one FIFO queue per `(db, key)` shared by *all* blocking commands watching that key. `NotifyWatchQueue()` only checked the front waiter: when its checker returned `kKeyNotFound` (e.g. `BLPOP`/`BZPOP*`/`BLMPOP` on a missing key), the scan aborted entirely and the one-shot wake event was cleared, so any *later* waiter in the same queue, from a different command family, was never checked at all. Concretely: a client blocked on `XREADGROUP` queued behind an earlier `BLPOP` waiter on the same key would never receive its `NOGROUP` error when the key was deleted. It stayed blocked indefinitely, only released later by an unrelated mutation of the key. ## Fix `NotifyWatchQueue` no longer aborts the whole scan on `kKeyNotFound`. It now tracks the checker (command family) that reported the key missing, and only fast-skips *later* waiters sharing that exact checker, this preserves the O (1)-per-item short-circuit from #7225 for the common homogeneous case (many `BLPOP` waiters on one absent key). Waiters from a different command family (e.g. `XREADGROUP` sharing a queue with `BLPOP`) are still probed individually, so they get the correct, immediate result instead of being hidden behind an unrelated waiter's outcome. ## Test plan - [x] New regression test `BlockingControllerTest.NotifyWatchQueueHeterogeneousCheckers`- two waiters with different checker types on one key's queue; the first reports `kKeyNotFound`, and the test asserts the second is still probed. - [x] Existing `BlockingControllerTest.NotifyWatchQueueFastPathOnAbsentKey` (the #7225 perf regression test) still passes unmodified, same-checker-type fast path is preserved. - [x] `blocking_controller_test`, `stream_family_test`, `list_family_test`, `zset_family_test` all passes. - [x] `pre-commit` (clang-format et al.) clean. Fixes #8067

signal.title: fix(zset): honor GT/LT flags for skiplist-encoded sorted sets
signal.text: ## Summary `ZADD ... GT` and `ZADD ... LT` were silently ignored once a sorted set left listpack encoding (i.e. once it had a member longer than 32 bytes, or more than 128 members). The score was overwritten unconditionally, as if the command were a plain `ZADD`, with no error. Root cause: the GT/LT clamp check exists in the listpack path (`ZsetAdd` in `zset_family.cc`) but was missing entirely from the skiplist path (`SortedMap::AddElem` in `sorted_map.cc`), which just updated the score whenever the element already existed. ## Fix Add the same GT/LT clamp to `SortedMap::AddElem`: if `LT` and the new score isn't lower, or `GT` and the new score isn't higher, treat the update as a no-op (matching the listpack path and Redis semantics). ## Test plan - Added `ZSetFamilyTest.AddGtLtSkiplist`, using a 33-byte member to force skiplist encoding immediately, covering both GT and LT in both the no-op and update directions. - `ninja zset_family_test && ./zset_family_test --gtest_filter='*GtLt*:*Add*'` — all 5 tests pass. - `pre-commit` clang-format check passes on both changed files. Fixes #8089
